biography:
Matt Bass, a name synonymous with unwavering consistency and calculated aggression in the Superkart 250cc scene, hails from the sun-drenched coastal town of Forster, Australia. Growing up, Matt wasn't exposed to the glitz and glamour of motorsport. His racing journey began humbly, tinkering with go-karts in his uncle's workshop, fueled by a fascination with speed and a knack for mechanical precision. His first taste of competition came at the local karting track, where he quickly earned a reputation for his smooth driving style and ability to extract every last ounce of performance from his machine.

After years honing his skills in karting, Matt made the transition to Superkart 250cc racing. The high speeds and technical challenges of Superkart proved to be a perfect fit for his skillset. While lacking the raw aggression of some of his rivals, Matt's meticulous preparation, unwavering focus, and exceptional tire management quickly made him a force to be reckoned with. A defining moment came in 2018 at the Phillip Island Grand Prix Circuit where, against all odds, he secured his maiden victory after a nail-biting final lap where the front runner crashed out. 

Now at 35, Bass finds himself in his career's prime. He is renowned as a steady and reliable driver, always bringing the kart home and steadily gaining points. While a championship remains elusive, he is a constant contender and a highly respected figure in the paddock, known for his sportsmanship and dedication to the sport. Although he has never won a championship, he has consistently been on the podium, making him a fan favourite.
drivingStyle: Matt's driving style is a masterclass in controlled aggression. He doesn't rely on flamboyant overtaking maneuvers or daring late-braking moves. Instead, he focuses on maintaining consistent lap times, preserving his tires, and capitalizing on the mistakes of others. He has an uncanny ability to read the track and anticipate changes in grip levels, allowing him to adapt his driving accordingly. His cornering technique is characterized by smooth, precise inputs and a focus on maximizing exit speed. He is also exceptional at managing tire wear, often gaining an advantage over his rivals in the closing stages of a race.

rivalries.reason: Ricardo's aggressive, unpredictable style clashes with Matt's calm approach, leading to several on-track incidents.
A fierce competitor, Thompson has often blocked Bass's path to victory, making their battles intense and strategic.
Nakamura and Bass have an ongoing rivalry stemming from a controversial collision that cost Bass a potential podium finish.

quirks: Always polishes his helmet visor with a microfiber cloth exactly five times before each race.
Listens to classical music (specifically Mozart) to calm his nerves before a race.
Refuses to start a race if his racing gloves are not perfectly aligned on the steering wheel.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't about being the fastest for a lap; it's about being consistently fast for every lap."
careerHighlight: Winning the 2018 Phillip Island Grand Prix after a thrilling last-lap overtake, marking his first major Superkart victory.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the final lap of the 2020 Bathurst 1000 Superkart race due to a mechanical failure, losing a certain victory.
